name: Eye whitening and brightening

card.summary: Efforts to make the whites of the eyes look whiter and brighter, discussed for contrast and a fresher look; little research targets this goal.
card.aka: White sclera, bright eyes, redness-reducing drops
card.note: Eye drops marketed for redness are a medical product category; users report trying them, and no study reviewed here tests them for appearance.

quick.overview:
Eye whitening and brightening refers to making the sclera (the white of the eye) look whiter and less red so the eyes appear fresher and higher in contrast. Users on looksmax.org describe white sclera and bright eyes as important for every eye colour because of contrast.

The sources found for this entry are thin. Published research reviewed is not about cosmetic eye whitening, so the article is short.
quick.mechanism: Proponents talk about reducing redness and the contrast between iris and sclera, and mention using eye drops. No studies reviewed examine how such methods affect perceived attractiveness.
quick.risks: Wikipedia's eye drop article does not cover redness-relieving drops in depth; it says alpha agonist drops used for glaucoma have a higher likelihood of allergic reaction and list burning, stinging and other side effects. Persistent redness is commonly a reason for medical review.

lead: Eye whitening and brightening is a looksmaxxing topic concerned with how white and clear the sclera looks and how bright the eyes appear. On looksmax.org, one user argued that sclera whiteness and brightness matter for every eye colour because of contrast, and said it is especially important for brown eyes; he asked others for ways to whiten the sclera and mentioned eye drops.[1]

No studies reviewed for this entry test cosmetic eye whitening or its effect on attractiveness, so the evidence is untested. General eye-drop information on Wikipedia notes that alpha agonist drops, a class used for glaucoma, are more likely to cause allergic reactions, and that the article does not discuss redness-relieving vasoconstrictor products in depth.[2]
infobox: Whiter sclera, less redness, brighter look

paras: In a looksmax.org thread, the original poster said that whiteness and brightness of the sclera matter for every eye colour because of contrast, and that it is mandatory for those with brown eyes; he said he used eye drops and asked for other suggestions.[1] Replies in the thread discussed makeup applied at the lateral canthus and its effect on perceived eye shape.[1]

Eye drops in general have a lower risk of side effects than oral medicines, and pressing on the inner corner of the eye briefly after instilling drops can reduce systemic absorption, according to Wikipedia.[2] Redness that lasts more than three days with lubricant drops is flagged there as a reason to consult a doctor.[2]

lore.intro: The topic appears in forum threads about eye contrast and perceived attractiveness.[1]

claims.claim: White sclera and bright eyes improve eye appearance through contrast.
claims.believers: A looksmax.org poster says sclera whiteness and brightness matter for every eye colour because of contrast, and especially for brown eyes.[1]
claims.experts: No published studies reviewed have tested whether sclera whiteness affects perceived attractiveness.

claims.claim: Eye drops can be used to whiten the sclera.
claims.believers: The same poster says eye drops can be used and asks for other whitening suggestions.[1]
claims.experts: No studies reviewed examine eye drops for cosmetic whitening; Wikipedia's general eye-drop article does not address redness-relieving products in depth.[2]
